title: Multimodal Agent Pipelines
summary: Combine text, images, audio, video, and structured observations while preserving modality-specific evidence and uncertainty.
overview: A multimodal agent pipeline coordinates extraction, alignment, interpretation, and validation across different forms of evidence. Its central architectural problem is not merely accepting an image alongside text; it is preserving the relationship between an assertion and the original region, timestamp, speaker, measurement, or document span that supports it.

Different modalities fail differently. OCR can lose a minus sign, audio transcription can confuse speakers, and image analysis can overlook an obscured object. Use modality-specific quality checks and retain uncertainty through fusion. A confident text summary must not erase the weaknesses of its underlying evidence.

production.poc: A proof of concept can inspect a small set of known files and manually verify extracted regions, timestamps, and source references.
production.production: Production requires validated media ingestion, bounded decoding, modality-specific quality checks, provenance links, and explicit abstention or human review for weak evidence.
production.scale: Enterprise scale adds asynchronous processing, artifact storage policy, modality-specific model routing, cost controls, accessibility requirements, and evaluation cohorts covering capture conditions and languages.

components.name: Media ingestion boundary
components.role: Validates file type, size, provenance, permissions, and parser safety before processing.

components.name: Specialist extractors
components.role: Produce OCR spans, audio segments, image regions, or structured measurements with quality metadata.

components.name: Alignment layer
components.role: Associates extracted observations by document, time, object, or task context without inventing missing links.

components.name: Evidence fusion agent
components.role: Builds a task-specific interpretation while retaining contradictions and source-level uncertainty.

components.name: Validation and review workspace
components.role: Lets humans inspect original regions or clips and approve consequential conclusions.

flow.title: Register source assets
flow.description: Assign immutable asset identities, access policy, capture metadata, and safe processing limits before decoding.

flow.title: Extract by modality
flow.description: Run suitable OCR, transcription, vision, or structured-data adapters and record model and preprocessing versions.

flow.title: Assess quality
flow.description: Detect unreadable pages, clipped audio, low-resolution regions, missing timestamps, or incompatible units before fusion.

flow.title: Align evidence
flow.description: Join observations using explicit identifiers and temporal or spatial references, marking ambiguous correspondences rather than forcing matches.

flow.title: Fuse bounded findings
flow.description: Generate claims with source anchors and uncertainty labels; keep conflicting modalities visible for review.

flow.title: Validate and publish
flow.description: Check critical fields deterministically where possible, request human inspection when needed, and retain the approved evidence manifest with the output.

useCase.title: Inspection evidence fusion
useCase.situation: Illustrative architecture: A quality engineer reviews a photographed defect, an operator voice note, and numeric inspection measurements for one production unit.
useCase.problem: The voice note references a different unit and the photograph does not show the measurement location clearly.
useCase.requirement: Combine useful evidence without silently treating all assets as describing the same object or proving a defect cause.
useCase.architecture: Extractors retain image coordinates and audio timecodes; alignment requires a verified serial identifier before the fusion agent creates an inspection packet.
useCase.failure: The audio serial number conflicts with the barcode in the image; the pipeline separates the assets and asks for identity clarification.
useCase.impact: Measure source-anchor coverage, critical-field accuracy, alignment errors, abstention quality, processing latency, and cost by modality and capture condition.

tradeoffs.cost: Add orchestration, intermediate artifacts, and latency.

tradeoffs.benefit: Can capture relationships across modalities directly.
tradeoffs.cost: May make individual extraction errors harder to localize.

tradeoffs.benefit: Supports consequential decisions when evidence is ambiguous.
tradeoffs.cost: Requires usable region and clip navigation and reviewer capacity.

failures.scenario: OCR changes a negative measurement into a positive value.
failures.detection: Numeric validation and image-region review disagree with the extracted field.
failures.recovery: Mark the field uncertain and require source verification before any calculation uses it.

failures.scenario: Audio and video timestamps drift during a long recording.
failures.detection: Alignment checks find increasing disagreement between synchronized reference events.
failures.recovery: Recalibrate the time mapping or split the recording into verified segments before fusion.

mistakes.mistake: Discarding original media after generating summaries.
mistakes.fix: Retain governed originals and source anchors for review and correction.

mistakes.mistake: Using one confidence score for the entire packet.
mistakes.fix: Track extraction quality, alignment certainty, and claim support separately.

mistakes.mistake: Letting visible or spoken instructions control agent tools.
mistakes.fix: Treat media content as untrusted evidence and enforce tool policy outside interpretation.

whenToUse: A task depends on relationships across images, documents, recordings, and structured records.
Reviewers need to inspect the exact source region or moment behind a claim.
Capture quality varies enough that uncertainty and abstention affect decisions.
whenNotToUse: A reliable structured data source already contains every required fact.
The workflow cannot retain or lawfully process the required media under its policies.
The consequence requires a certified sensor or professional assessment that model interpretation cannot replace.
checklist: Validate media type, size, permissions, and parser execution boundaries.
Preserve asset identity, source coordinates, timestamps, and preprocessing versions.
Evaluate extraction quality separately for each modality and capture condition.
Define explicit alignment keys and behavior for conflicting identifiers.
Carry uncertainty and contradictions through the final evidence packet.
Keep external media instructions outside the tool-authority boundary.
Provide source inspection and correction paths for consequential findings.
